message.content:
The most recent common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals.  
This ancestor lived roughly 100–110 million years ago, before the diversification of the major mammalian orders such as Carnivora (which contains lions) and Perissodactyla (which contains zebras).
